verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean's five bumps are `LocalizedMomentRepair.bump (cellLower a b j) (cellUpper a b j)` for j : Fin 2 (U) and j : Fin 3 (E), where (a,b) is the reserved positive radial patch, i.e. J_pos. Smoothness, nonnegativity and compact support in J_pos are stated (bump_contDiff, bump_nonneg, bump_support_subset, cell_union_subset). The normalization ∫_0^∞ b_j dR = 1 is not stated: searching the index for `bump_integral`, `normalizedBump` and for a bump lemma concluding `= 1` turns up only `OutgoingPulseBounds.power_bump_integral_scale` (a scaling identity) and `EulerSpatialCutoffs.normalizedBump` (Euler, out of scope, and normalized at the origin, not in integral). The recovery is a rescaling: each bump is continuous, nonnegative and equals 1 at the cell centre (bump_at_center), so its integral is a positive finite number c_j, and replacing b_j by b_j/c_j while replacing the coefficient by c_j·α_{n,j} leaves the repair function Σ_j α_{n,j} b_j — and hence (5.14) and the moment rows — unchanged; the Lean never uses the value of ∫b_j, since its coefficients are read off the inverse of the moment matrix (B)_ij = ∫ R^{p_i} b_j dR. One further encoding note: the Lean's U-cells (a 5-fold subdivision of (a,b)) and E-cells (a 7-fold subdivision) are each internally disjoint but are not disjoint from each other, unlike the paper's five mutually disjoint supports; the rows still split, since the axial rows see only the U-correction and the angular rows only the E-correction.
